items.title: Trading Your RRSP or Pension for the House: The After-Tax Math in a Divorce
items.summary: Swapping retirement savings for the family home is a common way to fund a spousal buyout. But a dollar in an RRSP isn’t worth a dollar of tax-free home equity, because tax comes off when the money is withdrawn. This guide works through the after-tax math with an example. It also explains how an RRSP can be moved to a spouse without tax using Form T2220, and why locked-in pension money changes the trade.Want to see what the buyout would cost in cash first? Try the free Matrimonial Home Buyout Calculator: https://divorcethesmartway.ca/tools/matrimonial-home-buyout/Ken S.
